newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firmer at outset, DAX seeks 3,700.
newsitem.headline: German shares firmer at outset, DAX seeks 3,700.

text.p: German shares were firmer in early trade on Friday, underpinned by overnight Wall Street gains and the firmer dollar, as the DAX index searched for strength to hurdle over 3,700 points in IBIS dealings.
The IBIS DAX was up 2.84 points at 3,687.44 points, while the DAX ended bourse trade on Thursday at 3,673.03 points.

The share market was waiting for the release at 0755 GMT of German unemployment data for May. But leaked data on Thursday showed ongoing high unemployment and has already been factored into the market, traders said.
Instead, the market is awaiting the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. unemployment data for May and its impact on Wall Street.
"We are looking at the U.S. right now for direction," said one share market trader.

The market's focus was on graphite and carbon maker SGL Carbon, which was slightly firmer after falling sharply overnight in the U.S. after saying it was among firms under investigation for alleged price fixing.
SGL shares were up 2.60 marks at 234.60 marks in pre-bourse trade after falling 4-3/4 to $46 in New York trading on speculation about the investigation by authorities.

The group, a former unit of Hoechst AG, said search warrants have been issued by U.S. and European Union authorities for company documents over allegations of price fixing among graphite electrode manufacturers.

Retailer Karstadt AG was down 4.50 marks at 620 marks in IBIS trade after reporting late on Thursday a decline in 1996 group net profit to 58.6 million marks from 109 million marks in 1995 but expressed confidence for 1997.
Metals group Preussag AG surged 12.50 marks to 492 marks on stake in new Venezuelan oil field and speculation it may take over travel and transport group Hapag Lloyd.
